notes: Works for the common case, but readZip decompresses every symlink member into memory with no size limit, even when --links is off; that is a DoS vector with a hostile archive and costs a remote read per symlink on S3. LinkRemote also wrongly skips the suffix for a symlink whose name already ends in .rclonelink. The new archiver helpers add surface the task did not need, and there are no squashfs tests.

The main zip and squashfs flows work, but there are real flaws: zip reads every symlink member eagerly and without a size bound during New, even when --links is off, which costs extra I/O and lets a crafted archive exhaust memory; LinkRemote leaves a symlink already named *.rclonelink unsuffixed, so it is misnamed on copy; OpenLink does not clamp negative offsets; and the squashfs single-file f.file switch to obj.Remote() is an unneeded, risky change; tests cover zip well, including a hostile copy, but squashfs has none.

Follows the reference closely: zip symlinks are skipped or suffixed and read the member content as the target, and squashfs stores the target and clamps offsets in Open. NewObject is kept consistent with List. Tests are thorough across zip, squashfs (binary fixture) and end-to-end copy/escape. Minor flaws: the nil,nil skip signal is unidiomatic, and a squashfs root pointing directly at a symlink leaves f.file unsuffixed.

Closely mirrors the reference: zip suffixes symlinks and reads the target lazily from the member, and squashfs exposes link targets with clamped range/seek and a NewObject fallback that keeps List and lookup consistent, including symlinks whose names already end in .rclonelink; there is a small link-only offset clamp hack in zip, and a squashfs single-file root pointing at a symlink isn't handled; tests are thorough across zip, squashfs (new binary fixture) and end-to-end copy/escape.

Fixes the root cause the same way as the reference: it collects `ph()` placeholder names from the checked CEL AST at provision time, treats non-literal names as dynamic, and retries on a response only for the exact response placeholders or the `http.reverse_proxy.header.` prefix. It covers every case the maintainers listed (shorthand and direct `ph`, upstream.host, escaped literals, lookalike names, dynamic names) with focused unit and integration tests; the only nit is that `PlaceholderNames()` returns the internal slice without cloning it.

Walks the checked CEL AST for `ph` calls at provision time. It records literal names and flags non-literal names as dynamic, then retries on a response only for expressions that read status, status text, response header or upstream latency placeholders (or a dynamic name). This covers every case the maintainers listed, and the tests at both the matcher and handler level are thorough. Minor nits: the getter returns the internal slice without cloning, and the `RetryMatchRaw` doc edit drops the mention of `{rp.is_transport_error}`.
